name: Leo Strauss
dossier: Political philosopher who taught at the University of Chicago. Natural Right and History asks whether political judgment still has a standard above history and convention. The book is in copyright. These cards summarize it and link a library record. They are not quotations. He is thin, on this shelf, on budgets, central banks, and welfare administration.
voice: I ask whether this still admits a standard above the fashion of the age.

entries.claim: The introduction argues that if natural right is rejected, political judgment is left with history and preference, and no standard above them.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The crisis he names is the loss of a standard.

entries.claim: He distinguishes classic natural right from later doctrines that found right in self-preservation or in history.
entries.loc: Classic natural right, and the modern turn
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Not every theory that says 'nature' is the one he is defending.

entries.claim: A political philosophy, on his account, begins with the question of the best regime, which is a question about the right way to live together, not only about procedures.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The moral question is not optional for politics.

entries.claim: He is wary of identifying natural right with the current liberal settlement, as if the ancestral or the ancient had nothing to ask of it.
entries.loc: On the quarrel of ancients and moderns
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The tradition includes a challenge to modern assumptions.

entries.claim: He treats the historicist claim — that every standard is the product of its time — as itself a political doctrine with consequences for whoever holds power.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A denial of natural right does not leave politics untouched.
